title: Recent advances in luminescent lanthanide based Single-Molecule Magnets
claim: Luminescent Er3+ SMMs are scarce because prolate Er3+ needs an equatorial field, often from organometallic ligands, and NIR emission is readily quenched by O–H, C–H, and C–N oscillators.
explanation: Despite many Er3+ SMMs and the technological interest of the NIR emission, antenna sensitization is described as usually difficult. Separate magnetism and luminescence are reported for beta-diketonate and tetrazole complexes. The only magneto-luminescent correlation cited is a 2D phosphonate polymer with pseudo-D5h Er3+, where the spectroscopic gap (31 cm−1) agrees with the ac barrier (24 cm−1), supporting Orbach relaxation.
scope: Er3+ SMMs, especially NIR-emissive coordination and organometallic complexes.
conditions: Equatorial crystal field for anisotropy; NIR excitation or antenna sensitization when non-radiative oscillators are controlled.
caveats: The good magnetic–optical agreement is a single cited example, not a broad series.
